newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's salt monopoly sold to former FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Austria's salt monopoly sold to former FinMin.

text.p: The Austrian government's industrial holding company OeIAG said on Monday it had awarded Austria's salt monopoly Salinen AG to a consortium led by former Austrian finance minister Hannes Androsch.
"The supervisory board of OeIAG has agreed to the sale of Salinen to the group of bidders (led by) Hannes Androsch," OeIAG said in a statement. "The group has offered the best price."
No financial details of the deal were available.

The group, which includes Upper Austrian regional bank Raiffeisen-Landesbank, was reported to have made a 700 million schillings offer which was said to have guaranteed jobs for the 350 workers and future investments of 450 million schillings.
Androsch was Austrian finance minister from 1976 to 1980 and has since been a prominent figure in the country's business community.

Sugar producer Agrana Beteiligungs-AG had put in a rival bid, which was widely tipped to win the race due to the group's domestic market experience and the entry it offered to the international market.

France's Compagnie des Salins du Midi, a unit of Morton International Inc, also had submitted a bid -- rumoured to be the biggest at 900 million schillings -- but only for Salinen's salt operations. Salinen also has interests in the property and tourism sectors.
The state put Salinen into the hands of state holding company OeIAG in August so that OeIAG could privatise the salt producer. OeIAG forecasts netting 500 million schillings from the sale.
In the first three quarters of the financial year ending on April 30, 1997, Salinen posted a loss of 41 million schillings but has forecast breaking even for the full year.
